issues.problem: No metric, no method, no outcome. I can't tell whether this was a Lighthouse tweak or a real bundle-splitting and rendering overhaul. In a pile of 120 frontend CVs, a claim with no number is treated as filler. It is also the only bullet that suggests the candidate delivers measurable results.
issues.fix: State what you measured, what you changed and the result, for example 'Cut LCP from 4.1s to 1.9s on the main app by code-splitting routes and lazy-loading images (React, Webpack)'. Do the same for the other bullets, adding a user, traffic or team-size number wherever you can.
issues.quote: Improved the performance of the main web app

issues.problem: This describes a duty, not what was done. It doesn't say how many projects, which stack, whether the candidate owned them alone or in a team, or whether they worked with designers, backend and QA. After about 5 years I can't judge whether this person can ship a feature by day 30 without hand-holding. 'Helped the juniors' and 'Worked on a React design system' are just as vague, and the design system line doesn't say what the candidate contributed.
issues.fix: Rewrite as specific deliverables: number and type of projects, tech used (React, TypeScript, testing, CI), your role, and the working setup (team size, code review, working with designers). For the design system, name what you built (components, tokens, Storybook, accessibility), how many components, and who adopted it.
issues.quote: Responsible for the frontend of several client projects

issues.problem: Belgian CV convention is no date of birth or age, and it invites bias. The language line also doesn't use CEFR levels, so 'native', 'very good' and 'basic' can't be compared with the A1-C2 scale Belgian employers expect. The other presentation choices (an emoji in the 'About me' heading, dot-rating bars for skills) look unpolished and the bars are self-assessed numbers nobody can verify.
issues.fix: Remove the date of birth. Write 'Dutch: C2 · English: C1 · French: A2' (use your real levels). Drop the emoji and replace the dot bars with a plain skills list grouped by use (React, TypeScript, CSS/Sass, Node.js), noting years of use or the project where you used each.

strength.quote: Worked on a React design system used by the whole team
strength.why: It is the one line that points to reusable, shared frontend work and to collaboration, and it fits a React scale-up team. It would carry real weight once it says what the candidate built and how many people or projects used it.
